topic: dtfile directory-entry packet framing and decoding

baseline_control.case: negative FileData2 field length passed to the production legacy decoder
baseline_control.result: AddressSanitizer rejected the legacy size conversion before the fix

coverage: valid and overflowing aggregate packing, including transactional failure
failed and successful symbolic-link stat classification
valid, negative-length, short-header and short-text record decoding
valid two-record packet, zero and oversized counts, trailing bytes and truncated second-record cleanup
source contracts for exact producer writes, bounded callback framing, malformed-response cleanup and unpacked non-pipe fallback

native_build.warnings: Only existing pointer-sign warnings in Desktop.c, assignment-condition warning in Directory.c and dangling-else warning in FileOp.c.

postconditions: make -n reports dtfile is up to date
no owned compiler, make, test or dtfile process remained before returning CPU2
the previously displayed directory is retained when a replacement packet is malformed
rejected_or_corrected_attempts: The first native pass named an exact Motif path that existed only on rpi4, so uconsole used fallback headers and the old libtool library input. That build was rejected; the complete prefix was transferred with byte, mode and symlink verification before recompilation.
A new null/initialization guard was initially inserted in the adjacent legacy reader and caused a compile failure. It was moved to ReadFileData2 before the passing build.
The first 13-case Linux test compile hid S_IFLNK under strict C11. The test compile now requests the same default-source feature namespace used by CDE; production code was unchanged.
limitations: This non-visual worker-protocol bundle did not launch or inspect a CDE window.
The standalone ldd invocation lacks build-tree paths for uninstalled CDE DSOs; only the verified Motif resolution is claimed.
